## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-expressible branchless blend over AoS particles can vectorize the integrate-decide-respawn loop and approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS layout offers 32 hot bytes in loop 1 (age+pos+seed+vel, 47%) and 28 in loop 2 (color+pos, 41%); the remaining 53–59% is dead weight per cacheline fill. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers, fusing integrate+decide+respawn into one pass. But the 68 B stride spans cacheline boundaries — every access pulls 64 B to touch 4–8 useful bytes. The approach uses select-based cmov logic, expecting the branchless blend to keep the pipeline full and amortize the dead-byte overhead.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across all regimes: at q=0.01, ns/p holds ~19–21 from L1d-resident (N=320) through DRAM (N=10M), a 10% spread with no knee at the L1d spill (~481), L2 spill (~7710), or L3 spill (~246K). A slight dip in L2/L3 (19.2 at N=99K vs 20.3 at N=320) reflects prefetch warmup; the only rise is DRAM at N≥370K (21.4). This flatness signals per-particle overhead, not cache capacity, as the bottleneck — the dense grid confirms no hidden cache-dependent regime change.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.5–3.5 GB/s — 20–28% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — against a 5.359 ns/p memory floor. The algo runs 19–27 ns/p, 3.5–5× above floor: not bandwidth-bound. Profile at N=10K, q=0.01 shows backend_stall 40.6%, compute 35.5%, branch_flush 22.0%; at q=0.5 compute rises to 42.3%, backend drops to 32.6%, but branch_flush holds ~23%. Branch- and overhead-bound throughout. Versus baseline: 0.76–0.92× (8–24% faster than naive). Versus the autovec winner: 1.4–2.8× slower — widest at q=0.01 (2.6–2.8×), narrowest at q=0.5 (1.4–1.5×) where respawn penalizes everyone.

## Assembly
Codegen did not vectorize the particle loop. The 17 vector instructions are mostly setup (vmovaps zeroing, vmovq color loads); the hot loop uses scalar FP — vmulss (×4), vaddss, vsubss, vcvttss2si — one particle at a time on stride-68B. The "branchless blend" became 13 conditional branches and 12 cmovb per iteration. Byte-granular scatter dominates: each color channel is loaded (movzx BYTE PTR), add-ed, clamped (cmovb), stored (mov BYTE PTR) — 19 scatters/iter. vpaddusb gives saturating adds but only ×2. At 160 insns/iter the core cannot retire fast enough to saturate memory.

## Verdict
Refuted — the branchless blend never materialized in codegen. Scalar FP with 13 conditional branches and 19 byte-granular scatters per iteration yields 0.76–0.92× of naive and 1.4–2.8× the winner's ns/p. At q=0.01, N=10K it is 2.6× slower than the autovec winner (19.8 ns/p, 0.80× of naive); at q=0.5 the gap narrows to 1.5× winner but branch_flush still holds at 23%. The scalar, scatter-heavy codegen cannot stream regardless of cache regime or death rate.
